parkex.11: In private car parks people drive through entire levels looking for a space, and spaces for people with disabilities get taken without a permit. ParkEx shows on each level's floor plan which spaces are free or occupied, and on reserved ones it reads the licence plate via OCR and checks whether it ends in DI, Uruguay's disability plate marker.
parkex.19: ParkEx architecture diagram: sensor and Arduino at the space, serial bridge and plate reader on the car park computer, REST API, PostgreSQL and Realtime on Supabase, and the browser

coded-bias.6: Speech, contact with the interviewees, dubbing of the English version and public presentation
coded-bias.8: It started as a documentary about gender equality and ended up asking a different question: if a society isn't equal, can the technology it builds be neutral? Two threads, one about machines and one about people, that come together at the end.
coded-bias.9: Structure of the documentary on the timeline: opening, intro, side A, side B, interviews and conclusion on video, with music on the audio track
escaneo.7: Java · ExecutorService · native ping and arp · com.sun.net.httpserver · bash
escaneo.9: A scanner that takes a network in CIDR notation, pings every address in parallel (up to 100 threads, 1 s timeout) and cross-checks the result with the ARP table to show IP, MAC and status. It has a web mode with POST /api/escanear and detects whether it runs inside Flatpak to execute commands on the host system.

escaneo.14: On Linux, reading the ARP table failed; it was solved with a script.
